# Introduction

The **`jjdotplotstats`** analysis (Horizontal Box-Violin Comparison) provides clinicopathological researchers and biostatisticians with intuitive, publication-ready tools in jamovi and R.

## Key Capabilities

- Compares a continuous variable across groups and draws the comparison horizontally - values on the x axis, group labels down the y axis - with an optional vertical reference line. Wraps ggstatsplot::ggbetweenstats and ggstatsplot::grouped_ggbetweenstats, so the figure is a box-violin plot with the individual observations shown, and the test is a between-groups comparison using every observation.  This analysis was previously titled "Dot Chart", which described neither the figure nor the statistic: it draws violins and boxplots, not a dot chart, and it is a between-groups test rather than a one-sample one. For a genuine Cleveland dot chart - one summary point per label, tested against a reference value - use "Dot Chart (Summary vs Reference Value)", which wraps ggstatsplot::ggdotplotstats.  Prefer this over "Box-Violin Plots to Compare Between Groups" when the group labels are long or numerous, since the horizontal layout gives them room, or when a clinical threshold line is useful.
- Seamless integration between jamovi graphical interface and automated R syntax generation.
- Rigorous handling of missing data, small cohorts, and multi-variable stratification.

# Example Workflow in R

```r
library(ClinicoPathJamoviModule)

# Load package test dataset
data("jjdotplotstats_test_data", package = "ClinicoPathJamoviModule", envir = environment())

# Run analysis with default settings
# ClinicoPathJamoviModule::jjdotplotstats(
#   data = jjdotplotstats_test_data
# )
```

# Clinical & Statistical Interpretation

Outputs generated by `jjdotplotstats` include summary tables, diagnostic indicators, and high-resolution plots tailored for oncology, pathology, and clinical trial reporting.
